title: Register Google Earth Engine
text:
Register Google Earth Engine
Google Earth Engine (GEE) is a cloud-based platform for geospatial analysis. To use it in the course Remote Sensing and Geodata Acquisition, you need to register a project for non-commercial use.
Prerequisites: A Google account (personal or institutional).







Figure 1: Go to code.earthengine.google.com and login with your google account. Choose I want to register a new product









Figure 2: Register for non-commercial use









Figure 3: Choose Private or academic institution









Figure 4: Under Check non-commercial eligibility: enter the full institution name (Zürcher Hochschule für Angewandte Wissenschaften), select No for payment, select Scientific research for use description, and enter your own research question.









Figure 5: Select Regional for geographic scope and specify your region. Select No for previously published work. You should see the message “Based on your answers, you are eligible for non-commercial Earth Engine use.” Click Next.









Figure 6: Under Choose your plan, select Community (intended for undergraduate students, no billing account required). Click Next.









Figure 7: Under Describe your work, check the categories that apply to your work and select a use case from the dropdown. Then click Register.









Figure 8: You should now see that your project is registered for non-commercial use









Figure 9: You should be redirected to the Earth Engine welcome page in Google Cloud Console, confirming your project is set up.









Figure 10: If you go to code.earthengine.google.com, your username should be blue, and not orange with a warning. If it is still orange, wait a few minutes and refresh — approval is usually instant but can take up to an hour.
